samples.summary: `toRgbHexColor` goes well beyond issue #728: a full CSS color normalizer (rgb()/rgba() parsing, #RGB expansion, #RRGGBBAA alpha handling, out-of-gamut clamping, transparency rules) is unrequested scope for a bug whose only acceptance criterion is "reset text color paints default ink, not the selection color" (docs/tasks/active/20260812-docs-font-color-reset-todo.md:104). Only the `''`→unset rule is needed for the issue; the rest silently changes existing DOCX/PPTX export output (e.g. `#abc` previously emitted verbatim as `abc`, now `AABBCC`; `#RRGGBBAA` previously passed through, now truncated/dropped) for documents unrelated to the reported bug.
samples.evidence: toRgbHexColor implements hex-3/6/8 + rgb()/rgba() parsing, clamping and alpha-drop rules; the issue's acceptance criterion concerns only canvas painting after a color reset.

samples.summary: The PPTX normalization is applied at one caller instead of at the single choke point that writes `<a:srgbClr val>`. `colorChildXml` (packages/slides/src/export/pptx/color.ts:35) still does only `replace(/^#/,'').toUpperCase()` and is also reached from shape fills, gradients, effects and theme slots (`solidFillXml`/`gradFillXml`/`effects.ts`), so the same invalid-`ST_HexColorRGB` class remains open on those sinks while `text.ts` grows a per-call guard. Guarding at `colorChildXml` would have expressed the invariant once, matching the diff's own "one shared normalizer, one convention" rationale.

samples.summary: A third export sink was left with its own duplicated color parsing. `styleColor` still hand-rolls `/^#?([0-9a-f]{6})$/` over `defaultColorResolver` output, so the CSS `rgb(...)` values the diff says are "routine" from HTML paste silently paint BLACK text in PDF export instead of the pasted color, and the new shared normalizer is not reused there. The task doc claims the normalizer "backs both export sinks" while a third one exists.

The "clearing a color means `undefined`, never `\"\"`" convention the diff establishes is applied to the two text-color toolbars but not to the docs table cell-background reset, which still writes `applyTableCellStyle({ backgroundColor: "" })` and therefore keeps storing the invalid empty-string attribute in the CRDT (the very root cause described in the task doc's Problem section). Non-goals exempt only the palette/picker UI and the highlight *rendering* path, not this reset site.

samples.summary: `toDocxHexColor` is a pure pass-through alias of `toRgbHexColor` (an exported function whose body is `return toRgbHexColor(color)`), adding an extra public name and its own test suite for zero behavior. Calling the shared helper directly from the two DOCX sinks would keep one name for one concept.

The change introduces a cross-package data-model invariant (`''` is a legacy "unset" color that every resolver/exporter must normalize) plus a new public API surface exported from both `@wafflebase/docs` entries and consumed by slides' PPTX exporter, but no design doc records it. `docs/design/docs/docs.md:102` still documents `color?: string; // hex, e.g. "#000000"`, and neither docs-docx-import-export.md nor slides/slides-pptx-export.md mentions the shared normalizer, so the convention lives only in a task file under docs/tasks/active/.

finding.summary: PPTX export only guards the `''` case, so the same invalid-OOXML class the delta fixes for DOCX remains for slides
finding.evidence: This delta argues (docx-style-map.ts:39-51, and the todo doc bullet "DOCX export normalizes the resolved color into a valid ST_HexColor") that `InlineStyle.color` may legitimately hold `rgb(…)` from HTML paste, `#abc`, `#RRGGBBAA`, or hostile junk, and that emitting such a value verbatim yields a document the consumer refuses to open. The PPTX sink is the identical shape but only got a `''` check: `hasColor` (text.ts:180) returns true for `'rgb(0, 128, 255)'`, and `colorChildXml` (packages/slides/src/export/pptx/color.ts:35) merely strips `#` and escapes, emitting `<a:srgbClr val="RGB(0, 128, 255)"/>` — not a valid `ST_HexColorRGB`. Slides text boxes go through the docs `TextEditor` (packages/slides/src/view/editor/text-box-editor.ts:34 imports from @wafflebase/docs) whose paste path calls `parseHtmlToBlocks` (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:1117), and that copies browser CSS colors verbatim (packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:151-154). So the reachable path the delta cites as the motivation for `toDocxHexColor` is left unfixed on the PPTX side. Additionally `hasColor` only tests the string arm, so the equivalent `{ kind: 'srgb', value: '' }` shape (explicitly acknowledged in packages/docs/src/model/color.ts:40-43 as reachable) still reaches `colorChildXml` and emits `val=""`, the exact output the new guard exists to prevent.

verdict.reason: The code the finding describes does not exist. There is no `hasColor` helper anywhere in the source tree (a repo-wide grep matches only the `.agent-review/correctness/stage-detail.json` review artifact), and the PPTX text sink is NOT limited to an `''` check. `packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:183-200` defines `storedColorToThemeColor`, which normalizes both the bare-string arm and the `{ kind:'srgb', value }` arm through the shared `toRgbHexColor` (imported from `@wafflebase/docs` at text.ts:3) and returns `undefined` — dropping the color child — whenever the value is not expressible as six hex digits; the role arm is validated against `ROLE_TO_SCHEME` with a black fallback. All inline-style color sinks route through it before reaching `colorChildXml`: `s.color` (text.ts:281-284), `s.backgroundColor` → `<a:highlight>` (287-290), `s.underlineColor` → `<a:uFill>` (293-298), and `marker.color` → `<a:buClr>` (135-138). `toRgbHexColor` (packages/docs/src/model/color.ts:89-116) is the same normalizer `toDocxHexColor` delegates to (packages/docs/src/export/docx-style-map.ts:47-49) and it handles `rgb()/rgba()`, `#abc`, `#RRGGBBAA`, transparent alpha, and falsy/`''` input (line 90). So `'rgb(0, 128, 255)'` becomes `val="0080FF"` and `{kind:'srgb',value:''}` is dropped rather than emitting `val=""` — the reuse the finding asks for is already in place on the PPTX side.
